references.text: Parallel passage in Matthew: 'Whoever acknowledges me before men, I will also acknowledge him before my Father in heaven' ([ref:Matt 10:32|Matthew 10:32]). This is the closest parallel to Jesus' words in Luke, but with the difference that Matthew says 'my Father in heaven' while Luke says 'God's angels'.

In the letter to Sardis, Jesus promises: 'The one who conquers... I will confess his name before my Father and before his angels' ([ref:Rev 3:5|Revelation 3:5]). Here the same motif of confessing someone's name before the Father and the angels is used, which connects to the promise in Luke 12:8.

Paul writes that 'if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord... you will be saved' ([ref:Rom 10:9-10|Romans 10:9-10]). Confessing Jesus before people as a path to salvation is the same principle Jesus speaks about.

'If we endure, we will also reign with him. If we deny him, he will also deny us' ([ref:2 Tim 2:12|2 Timothy 2:12]). This reflects both the promise in Luke 12:8 and the warning in the next verse (12:9) that whoever denies Jesus will themselves be denied.
John writes: 'Whoever confesses the Son has the Father also' ([ref:1 John 2:23|1 John 2:23]). Confessing the Son before people is connected to eternal fellowship with God, as described in Luke 12:8.

'Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God' ([ref:1 John 4:15|1 John 4:15]). Confessing Jesus as a mark of genuine faith connects to Jesus' promise to confess the believer before God's angels.

The immediately following verse forms the counterpart: 'But whoever denies me before men, I will also deny him before the angels of God' ([ref:Luk 12:9|Luke 12:9]). Together the verses form a contrast pair about confession versus denial.

Jesus says: 'Whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of them when he comes in his glory and the glory of the Father and of the holy angels' ([ref:Luk 9:26|Luke 9:26]). The motif of the Son of Man, the angels, and the eschatological confession is the same as in 12:8.

Parallel passage in Mark: 'Whoever is ashamed of me and my words... the Son of Man will also be ashamed of them when he comes in his Father's glory with the holy angels' ([ref:Mark 8:38|Mark 8:38]). The title Son of Man and the presence of the angels at judgment are common motifs.
